findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses flat fields with no enforced lifecycle state machine. mark_sent can be called at any time, producing invalid transitions (e.g. sent without validated, re-sent, or status overwritten after terminal state).
findings.failure_mode: illegal states are representable: a RouteWorkflow can hold status='sent', is_sent=true, is_validated=false simultaneously, or be marked sent multiple times with no guard
findings.fix: Replace the struct with a typestate enum such as enum RouteState { Unvalidated { id: RouteId, sent_at: Option<u64> }, Sent { id: RouteId, sent_at: u64 } } so transitions compile away from invalid combinations.

findings.problem: status is a public String field. Any caller can set it to any string value (empty, 'deleted', 'cancelled', etc.) with no domain validation, and no variant distinguishes the meaning.
findings.failure_mode: callers bypass domain invariants by assigning arbitrary strings; pattern matching on status requires string comparison instead of exhaustive enum match; typos produce silent logical bugs
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `enum RouteStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` so only valid states are representable and match is exhaustive.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent booleans encoding lifecycle. They can be in contradictory combinations (e.g. validated=false, sent=true) that violate domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: any 2^4=16 combinations of (is_validated, is_sent, status, sent_at) are representable, including impossible states like a route that is sent but not validated
findings.fix: Collapse booleans into a single typestate enum with explicit variants (e.g. `enum RouteLifecycle { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`) so each variant owns exactly the data it needs.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a standalone field. A route can be sent without a timestamp (sent_at=Some missing while is_sent=true) or have a timestamp without being marked sent, both logically inconsistent.
findings.failure_mode: optional lifecycle data is decoupled from the lifecycle state, allowing sent routes without timestamps and non-sent routes with timestamps — callers must check two fields for every invariant
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms inside the Sent variant: `Sent { id: RouteId, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` so the timestamp is always present when the route is sent and absent otherwise.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics. Callers can pass empty strings, arbitrary lengths, or non-unique values. There is no compile-time distinction between a RouteId and any other string.
findings.failure_mode: domain invariants on IDs (format, length, uniqueness) cannot be enforced at the type level; any String-producing code is accepted as a valid id
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct RouteId(String);` with a smart constructor `RouteId::try_from(s: &str) -> Result<RouteId, InvalidIdError>` and use it as the id field type.

findings.problem: There is no parse boundary. Raw String and bool primitives are accepted directly by the public struct and function. No smart constructor validates or transforms hostile inputs before the core consumes them, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: any caller passes arbitrary primitives and the core logic operates on potentially invalid data; no fallible smart constructor enforces domain invariants at the boundary
findings.fix: Add a module-level `Route::try_new(id: &str, initial_state: RouteState) -> Result<Route, ParseError>` that validates inputs, creates the domain type, and ensures only the typestate enum exposes the core.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes RouteWorkflow by value and mutates fields in place. There is no separation between pure calculation (state transition logic) and shell (mutation). The function has no typed return for validation failures and silently overwrites state.
findings.failure_mode: no error path — calling mark_sent on an already-sent or unvalidated route silently produces an invalid state; no pure calculation is isolated from mutation
findings.fix: Return `Result<RouteWorkflow, TransitionError>` with exhaustive match on the typestate enum; implement mark_sent as a pure function from one valid state to another, returning a typed error for illegal transitions.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, allocation, or second-ring command evidence exists. mark_sent calls `.to_string()` on line 10 which allocates a new String. No allocation budget, allocation evidence, or performance measurement is provided.
findings.failure_mode: allocation behavior of mark_sent (String::to_string on every call) is unmeasured; in a high-throughput path this per-call allocation could be a measurable bottleneck with no evidence to justify or optimize it
findings.fix: Add a criterion benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocations and latency; replace `status = "sent".to_string()` with a pre-allocated or enum-based approach once measured; include allocation count in the benchmark output.

missing_evidence: no benchmark for mark_sent allocation behavior (String::to_string on every call)
no profiler data for hot-path analysis
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence
no command evidence (cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test) was executed
no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claims
no typestate transition test suite proving illegal states are unrepresentable
residual_risk: The crate has fundamental architectural violations: no typestate enforcement, no parse boundary, no typed error taxonomy, and raw primitive domain fields. The struct can represent every illegal state combination. All 8 findings are blockers that must be resolved before any delivery. No commands were run so compile-time and test-gate status is unknown. Without typestate, no proof of panic-freedom or invariant enforcement is possible.
